sentences.en: At nine o'clock this morning, the company had an important meeting.
I got to the company very early to prepare things for the meeting.
When the meeting started, Xiao Wang hadn't arrived yet, and the manager was a little unhappy.
Ten minutes later, Xiao Wang finally ran in, saying sorry while sitting down.
We discussed next month's work plan at the meeting.
The manager said this plan was important, and hoped everyone would work hard to do it well.
After the meeting ended, we all felt this meeting was very useful.

quiz.q: What happened when the meeting started?
a: Xiao Wang hadn't arrived yet and the manager was a little upset

quiz.q: What did they discuss at the meeting?
How did they feel after the meeting?
a: They felt the meeting was very useful
They felt tired and wanted to sleep
They felt the meeting was too long

grammar.p: 一边……一边…… (doing two things at once)
grammar.e: 一边 + verb1，一边 + verb2 describes two actions happening at the same time.
grammar.x: 小王才跑进来，一边说对不起，一边坐下。 — Xiao Wang finally ran in, saying sorry while sitting down.

grammar.e: 还没有 (or 还没) before a verb shows that an action hasn't happened yet, even though it was expected.
grammar.x: 会议开始的时候，小王还没有来。 — When the meeting started, Xiao Wang hadn't arrived yet.

grammar.e: 希望 can be directly followed by a full clause describing what someone hopes will happen.
grammar.x: 经理说，这个计划很重要，希望大家都努力做好。 — The manager said this plan was important, and hoped everyone would work hard to do it well.
